attempts.paper_title: Reactivations of emotional memory in the hippocampus–amygdala system during sleep
attempts.entry_title: Hippocampus-amygdala reactivations during sleep (Girardeau et al. 2017)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's main findings held up in this data. Hippocampus-BLA pairs reactivated in NREM but not REM sleep after training, less so for piriform cortex and not for the central nuclei, ripple-modulated BLA cells contributed most, and the air puff trajectory was reactivated around ripples. The sleep states are not deposited, so these results rest on states decoded from the authors' firing-rate tables, and several change under other decoder settings. The rats' learning of the daily danger zone held up only in part, as the air puff location is deposited for 6 of 55 sessions and had to be estimated. A control finding no bias from that location did not reproduce.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Girardeau, Inema and Buzsaki (2017) on CRCNS hc-14, which holds the sorted spikes, positions and events of 4 rats recorded in dorsal CA1 and the amygdala during an aversive linear track task and sleep, and the authors' summary tables. It covers the behaviour, the firing rates per sleep state, the hippocampus-BLA reactivation and its cell and pair groups, and, on sleep states decoded from the authors' state firing rates, the reactivation strength around ripples.

findings.statement: The hand-scored sleep states (NREM, REM, wake intervals) are not deposited, nor the run intervals and lap classifications the analyses used. Rescoring states from the LFP would mean streaming 461 GB of tar.gz archives; this attempt decoded them from the per-state firing rates of the StatesFR table, which reproduces the authors' NREM and REM pair correlations closely but not exactly.

The summary tables in AllRats-Variables.tar.gz (FinalType, StatesFR, SpikeParameters, PoissonRippleMod, EVcontribs, AllRippleCCGs) are undocumented, as the data description says. Their columns could be identified against the raw spikes, except which StatesFR column is REM (column 5 or 8).

The structure of each shank and day comes in four formats, one per rat (Structures/*.mat for Rat09 and Rat10, Structures.txt for Rat11, Batch-Files/Structures.batch and StructureMapping.ods for Rat08). Rat08's labels other than BLA are only in the All sheet of the ods, with spellings that differ from the other rats (CeC and CeM for CeCM, PIr, mixed labels such as VEn/Pir); Rat08 sessions 10 to 13 list no BLA shanks, and the hippocampal shanks are listed only for Rat10.
Rat08-20130722 has 152 sorted units in its clu files and 127 in the summary tables (28 only in the clu files, 3 only in the tables); the other 60 sessions agree unit for unit.
The bucket holds 65 sessions; the paper's 61 are listed only in sessionindexing.mat. Rat11-20150309, -0318, -0319 and -0324 are left out without a stated reason.

Only 6 of the 55 behaviour sessions carry an airpuffloc file with the air puff location and direction; for the others they must be inferred from the head position at the air puffs, which lies -3 to 18 cm (median 7.3 cm) past the file's location in the direction of travel where both exist. Several behaviour outcomes change with a 7.3-cm correction.

The pair table's run correlations match correlations recomputed over the run subsession in 17 of 29 sessions (r > 0.999) and less well in 12 (r = 0.58 to 0.98), so the run interval the authors used is not the run subsession in those sessions and is not deposited.

Question for the authors. Which StatesFR column is REM? This attempt took column 5 over column 8; epochs decoded as column 5 give hippocampus-BLA pair correlations that follow the table's REM correlations (r about 0.8), which supports it. With column 8 the REM/wake ratios of BLA cells would be smaller than the NREM/wake ratios, against Figure 2c.

Question for the authors. Was the air puff location of BehavioralMeasures.m taken from the airpuffloc files, from the puff events, or from elsewhere, and where is it for the 49 sessions without an airpuffloc file? This attempt used the median head position at the air puffs, and the location-bias test (airpuff-location-no-bias) depends on it.

The session archives are tar.gz files without an index, and each clu archive (0.1 to 2.5 GB) is mostly RawKK, .fet and .klg files; reading the sorted spikes of one session means decompressing the whole archive (99 GB over 65 sessions), and the 65 LFP archives are 3.0 to 9.0 GB each (461 GB).
Rat08's two structure lists disagree on one shank-day: StructureMapping.ods labels shank 13 of session 5 (Rat08-20130712) BLA, and Structures.batch does not list it.

In Rat10-20140622 the hippocampal cells of the pair table (shanks 17 to 20) fire no spike over a 20-min stretch of decoded post-sleep NREM, while the session's BLA cells fire 31,040 spikes in it; the hippocampal spikes of that stretch are missing from the clu files, or the hippocampal shanks stopped recording.

entries.title: Hippocampus-amygdala reactivations during sleep (Girardeau et al. 2017)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Girardeau, Inema and Buzsaki (2017) on CRCNS hc-14, which holds the sorted spikes, positions and events of 4 rats recorded in dorsal CA1 and the amygdala during an aversive linear track task and sleep, and the authors' summary tables. It covers the behaviour, the firing rates per sleep state, the hippocampus-BLA reactivation and its cell and pair groups, and, on sleep states decoded from the authors' state firing rates, the reactivation strength around ripples.
